hypothesis: The already-measured coalesced one-output-per-thread control was correct and averaged 0.0234084 s, versus the baseline's 0.2734839 s. A 16x32 output tile with K depth 32 should preserve column-coalesced lanes while reusing each staged A value across 32 outputs and each B value across 16 outputs. The larger K chunk may amortize synchronization, though shared-memory traffic and the 512-thread CTA could offset gains; this candidate still needs controller correctness checks and repeated timing.
notes: This proposal uses synchronous shared memory, full-FP32 accumulation, one output per thread, column-varying lanes, and masked tails. It leaves scratch unused and launches on the existing default stream. No correctness or timing result is claimed for this new candidate; the controller should establish both and report repeated samples.
transformations: Replaced the serial per-output global-memory K loop with synchronous CTA staging of 16x32 A and 32x32 B tiles at K depth 32.
Mapped threadIdx.x across 32 output columns, with one thread accumulating and storing one output.
Masked global loads and stores for matrix tails; used size_t offsets and quotient/remainder tile counts.
Kept the existing run entry point, alpha/beta update, default-stream launch, and unused scratch buffer; introduced no allocation or external math-library call.
